introH2: 🏙️ What kind of stays does the Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: If you want a Chiang Mai stay where you can wake up and stroll the night market, then come back to sleep in a plush riverfront room the same evening, the Night Bazaar/Chang Klan and Ping riverside area is the answer — Chang Klan Road is the heart of the Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market, while the bend of the Ping River on the Wat Ket and Charoen Prathet side is lined with luxury resorts under big shade trees · what sets this area apart is the sheer variety of stays in one location — five-star big-chain hotels, design-led riverfront resorts, a century-old teak heritage house, romantic boutiques, all the way to riverside boutiques in the low-four-figure baht range · a common problem is booking on pretty photos and ending up with a room facing the lively Chang Klan Road at night, or choosing a beautiful riverside spot so far out you can't walk to the market · this article rounds up 10 stays in the Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area we've reviewed in depth, working down from big-chain hotels in the city centre to light-budget riverside boutiques — every one based on reading real guest reviews, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Chiang Mai has no metro, but the Night Bazaar/Chang Klan area is right in the city and walkable · calling a Grab or hopping on a red truck (songthaew) is easy and cheap · from Chiang Mai airport (CNX) into the Chang Klan area takes about 10–15 min · the main landmarks in the area: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market on Chang Klan Road — a lively night market every evening, with many of the stays on this list within a 3–10 min walk · the bend of the Ping River on the Wat Ket and Charoen Prathet side — a leafy riverside setting, with several resorts a bridge-crossing away from the Night Bazaar side · Tha Phae Gate and the Old City are about a 5–10 min drive away · note: Raya Heritage sits on the Ping River in the Mae Rim area outside the city, about a 15–20 min drive into town, and you can't walk to the night market.

entries.type: Luxury City Hotel 5★ · heart of the Night Bazaar
entries.name: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · from over 1,000 real reviews · ranks among the top in Chiang Mai
entries.badge: 📍 walk out of the lobby to the Night Bazaar · infinity pool with mountain views
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chang Klan Road · heart of the Night Bazaar · walk to Anusarn Market
tags: 🏊 infinity pool with Doi Suthep views
entries.addr: 108 Chang Klan Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If you had to pick one stay that fits this area most completely, the honest takes from real reviews lean fairly clearly toward Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel · it's a high-rise in the middle of Chang Klan Road where you step out of the lobby into the Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market, but ride the lift up to the podium level and find a quiet infinity pool with Doi Suthep as its backdrop · many people still call it Le Meridien from before it rebranded into the Marriott group. It's a five-star hotel with 383 rooms, starting around ฿4,500/night, scoring 9.3 from over 1,000 reviews — the most on this list, which reflects that it's been proven by a large number of guests · the highlight is the value of a big-chain hotel in the heart of the Night Bazaar, with a Club Lounge on floors 21–22 with mountain views for Bonvoy members · the honest caveats from the reviews: rooms facing Chang Klan Road or on lower floors pick up the nightlife noise, the breakfast queue is long at peak times when the hotel is full, and being a big hotel, service can feel less personal than at a boutique · but if you want a location in the middle of the night market, a pool with mountain views and reliable chain standards, Marriott is number one on this list.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a high-floor mountain-view room at the time of booking, since the Doi Suthep view is the highlight and it also escapes the Chang Klan Road noise better · go down for breakfast right when it opens or near the end of service to avoid the long queue · and if the room rate works out, try upgrading to a Club Room to use the Club Lounge on floors 21–22.
pros: Location in the heart of the Night Bazaar, walk out of the lobby to the night market and Anusarn Market
Podium-level infinity pool with Doi Suthep views · reliable Marriott chain standards
The most reviews on this list, over 1,000, proven by a large number of guests
Club Lounge on floors 21–22 with mountain views, ideal for Marriott Bonvoy members (from the reviews)
cons: Rooms facing Chang Klan Road or on lower floors pick up the nightlife noise
Breakfast queue is long at peak times when the hotel is full
Being a big hotel, service can feel less personal than at a small boutique

entries.name: Anantara Chiang Mai Resort
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · from real reviews · design-led riverfront resort
entries.badge: 🌊 on the Ping River · Kerry Hill design · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Charoen Prathet Road · on the Ping River · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 123-123/1 Charoen Prathet Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Anantara Chiang Mai Resort is a riverfront resort that does two things at once that usually mean choosing one or the other — walk a few minutes out of the lobby and you reach the Night Bazaar, but come back in and it's quiet as if it were a different world · designed by architect Kerry Hill on the former grounds of the British Consulate, its clean, dignified lines blend Lanna and contemporary in a way many reviews call the most beautiful design on the Ping riverside · it has 84 rooms and suites starting around ฿8,500/night, scoring 9.2 · the highlights people mention are the calm atmosphere on the Ping River, the long swimming pool, and afternoon tea in the 1921 House, the former British Consulate building · the honest caveats from the reviews: prices are above the area average, with only 84 rooms it fills fast in high season, lower-floor rooms on the Charoen Prathet Road side pick up some street noise, and afternoon tea seating is limited and must be booked ahead · it suits people who want a design-led riverfront luxury resort that still lets you walk to the night market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a higher-floor Deluxe River View, since the Ping River view is worth the difference and helps escape the Charoen Prathet Road noise · book afternoon tea at the 1921 House ahead, since it's served on weekdays and seating is limited · and if you come Nov–Feb, lock in a free-cancellation room early, since river-view rooms fill fast.
pros: Design-led Kerry Hill riverfront resort on the Ping River, quiet yet walk to the Night Bazaar
Leafy atmosphere, a long swimming pool, Anantara-level service
Afternoon tea in the former British Consulate building, the 1921 House
Spacious rooms from 50 sqm with garden or river views (from the reviews)
cons: Prices are above the area average
Only 84 rooms, fills fast in high season
Lower-floor rooms on the Charoen Prathet Road side pick up some street noise · afternoon tea seating is limited

entries.type: Luxury Boutique Hotel 5★ · teak heritage house
entries.name: 137 Pillars House
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.5 · from real reviews · the highest score on this list
entries.badge: 🏛️ Small Luxury Hotels · a teak house over 140 years old
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wat Ket · Ping riverside · ~5–10 min to the Night Bazaar
tags: ✨ Small Luxury Hotels of the World
entries.addr: 2 Nawatgate Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: 137 Pillars House is the stay many reviews say redefines what luxury means in Chiang Mai, and it's the highest-scoring on this list at 9.5 · open the door and you find a dark-brown teak house with high roofs and long verandas, over 140 years old, standing in a quiet garden by the Ping River in the Wat Ket area — not a glass tower but a heritage of the teak-trading era, meticulously restored · it's a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World with 30 suites, the smallest starting at 70 sqm with a private veranda, from around ฿18,000/night · the highlights are the high level of privacy, the refined service, and the calm riverside garden setting · the honest caveats from the reviews: it's the highest-priced on this list, it sits on the Wat Ket side so you take a car or walk about 5–10 min across to the Night Bazaar side, with only 30 suites it fills fast, and as a small boutique it doesn't have the facilities of a big hotel · this isn't a pick for a tight budget, but if you're after the most luxurious and characterful stay on the Ping riverside for a special occasion, 137 Pillars House is that mark.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: it suits a special-occasion trip, so book several weeks ahead since there are only 30 suites · if you want to explore the night market, use the hotel's car service or a Grab across to the Chang Klan side, since the Wat Ket side is quieter · and allow time for afternoon tea in the teak garden, which is the prettiest light of the day.
pros: The highest score on this list, 9.5 · a teak heritage house over 140 years old with real character
Member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World · refined, personal service
All-suite, the smallest at 70 sqm with a private veranda
A quiet garden by the Ping River in the Wat Ket area, ideal for a special occasion (from the reviews)
cons: The highest price on this list, from ฿18,000/night
On the Wat Ket side, you take a car or walk 5–10 min across to the Night Bazaar side
Only 30 suites, fills fast · a small boutique without the facilities of a big hotel

entries.name: Na Nirand Romantic Boutique Resort
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · from real reviews · a romantic riverside stay
entries.badge: 🌳 100-year-old rain tree by the river · Colonial-Lanna design
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Charoen Prathet Soi 9 · on the Ping River · Chang Klan
entries.addr: 1/1 Soi 9 Charoen Prathet Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Na Nirand Romantic Boutique Resort is a resort many reviews call one of the most beautiful romantic stays in Chiang Mai · walk down a small lane by the Ping River in the Chang Klan area and you meet a huge rain tree over 100 years old, its branches spreading over the garden, with a Colonial-meets-Lanna building set in its shade and the Ping River drifting past behind · the design draws on the teak-trading era of King Rama V's reign, with rooms from 31–36 sqm, from around ฿3,900/night, scoring 9.3 · the highlights people mention are the riverside atmosphere under the rain tree and the free afternoon tea for two, served at the prettiest light of the day, ideal for couples and honeymoons · it's a riverside location that still lets you walk to the Night Bazaar area · the honest caveats from the reviews: some nights carry music from a bar across the river, standard Deluxe rooms don't have a river view so you'd need to upgrade to a Riverfront Suite, and being a romance-focused boutique, it doesn't suit families with young children running around · it suits couples wanting a pretty riverside setting at a more reachable price than the area's other luxury resorts.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're celebrating a special occasion and want a river view, choose the 65–73 sqm Riverfront Colonial Suite, the signature room that looks straight out at the Ping River · don't miss the free afternoon tea under the rain tree in the afternoon · and if you're sensitive to noise, tell the front desk you'd like a room not facing the bar side at the time of booking.
pros: Romantic atmosphere on the Ping River under a 100-year-old rain tree, Colonial-Lanna design
Free afternoon tea for two by the river, at the prettiest light of the day
More reachable price than the area's other luxury resorts, walk to the Night Bazaar
Ideal for couples and honeymoons, attentive service (from the reviews)
cons: Some nights carry music from a bar across the river
Standard Deluxe rooms don't have a river view, you'd need to upgrade to a Riverfront Suite
Romance-focused, not ideal for families with young children

entries.name: Cross Chiang Mai Riverside
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · from real reviews · design-led all-suite
entries.badge: 🏊 rooftop infinity pool over the Ping bend · MICHELIN Guide
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wat Ket · Ping riverside · cross the bridge, 5–10 min to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 369/1 Charoenrajd Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Cross Chiang Mai Riverside (formerly X2 Chiang Mai Riverside) is an all-suite five-star hotel many people talk about for rooms bigger than expected and sharp design · the modern building with clean, crisp lines stands quietly on the Ping River in the Wat Ket area, and up on the rooftop you find an infinity pool whose edge meets the horizon, looking straight out over the Ping bend, prettiest at sunset · it's a MICHELIN Guide member with 29 suites, rooms from 51 sqm with a private balcony, from around ฿4,200/night, scoring 9.2 · the Wat Ket location is a 5–10 min walk across the bridge to the Night Bazaar side · the honest caveats from the reviews: with only 29 suites it fills fast in high season, Garden View rooms see the garden or a building rather than the river so choose River View if you want the water, and being on the Wat Ket side you cross the bridge or call a car to the night market · it suits people who value a spacious suite, design and a rooftop pool over the river at a price that's good value for a five-star.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: go up to the rooftop infinity pool at sunset, when the view over the Ping bend is at its best — order a drink at the pool bar and take in the city view · ask for a River View or Grand Suite at the time of booking, since Garden View sees the garden or a building instead · and allow about 5–10 min to walk across the bridge to the Night Bazaar in the evening.
pros: All-suite with spacious rooms from 51 sqm and a private balcony, sharp design
Rooftop infinity pool over the Ping bend, prettiest at sunset
MICHELIN Guide member · good value for an all-suite five-star
Riverside Wat Ket location, walk across the bridge to the Night Bazaar (from the reviews)
cons: Only 29 suites, fills fast in high season
Garden View rooms see the garden or a building instead of the river, choose River View
On the Wat Ket side, you cross the bridge or call a car to the night market

entries.type: City Hotel 5★ · Chang Klan · great value
entries.name: The Empress Premier Chiang Mai
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.0 · from real reviews · great-value five-star near the Night Bazaar
entries.badge: 💸 five-star 40 sqm rooms from the low thousands · near the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chang Klan · Charoen Prathet Soi 12 · walk to the Night Bazaar
tags: 🚶 walk to the Night Bazaar and Anusarn
entries.addr: 199/42 Soi Charoenprathet 12, Changklan Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: In a city where five-star riverfront hotels usually come with five-figure prices, The Empress Premier Chiang Mai is the choice many people talk about because you get rooms starting at 40 sqm, an outdoor pool and an Executive Lounge from the low thousands · it's a new building that opened in 2019 in the Chang Klan area, a walk to the Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market, with 138 rooms and suites from around ฿2,400/night, scoring 9.0 · the selling point is space and value over trendy design, suiting families and anyone who wants five-star standards on a reasonable budget in the middle of the night market area · the honest caveats from the reviews: the name is easy to confuse, since this is a different, newer building from the original The Empress Hotel — check for the word Premier when booking — some reviews mention air-con noise and sound carrying from the next room, breakfast options are limited, and the décor is plain rather than design-forward · but if the brief is a five-star with spacious rooms near the Night Bazaar at the best value among the big hotels, this hits it squarely.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: check for the word Premier when booking, since this is a different, newer building from the original The Empress Hotel · ask for a high floor and avoid rooms by the street or common areas to escape air-con noise and sound from the next room · and if breakfast options feel limited, choosing a room-only rate and eating around Anusarn/Chang Klan may be better value.
pros: Five-star with rooms from 40 sqm, a pool and an Executive Lounge from the low thousands
New building from 2019 in the Chang Klan area, walk to the Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market
Focus on space and value, suits families
Best value among the big hotels near the night market (from the reviews)
cons: Name is confusing with the original The Empress Hotel, check for the word Premier when booking
Some reviews mention air-con noise and sound carrying from the next room
Limited breakfast options · plain décor rather than design-forward

entries.name: Rati Lanna Riverside Spa Resort
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.9 · from real reviews · good-value Lanna luxury on the river
entries.badge: 🌊 on the Ping River · daybed balconies · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chang Klan Road · on the Ping River · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 33 Changklan Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Rati Lanna Riverside Spa Resort is a resort many people choose for Lanna-style luxury at a more reachable price than the area's other riverfront resorts · walk a few minutes and you reach the Night Bazaar, but come back through the gate and it's calm and quiet, with big trees, a long swimming pool and room balconies facing the Ping River · the décor uses local wood and woven textiles, rooms from 40–60 sqm, many with a daybed balcony, from around ฿4,500/night, scoring 8.9 · the highlights are the riverside resort atmosphere, the spa and the good-value daybed balconies for a five-star, suiting people who want Lanna riverside luxury on a reasonable budget · the honest caveats from the reviews: it has fewer reviews than the area's bigger names, parts of the building and décor are starting to age with use, and the entry-priced standard rooms have a garden view rather than a river view — you'd need to upgrade to River View for the water · it suits couples and families wanting a riverside resort with a spa near the night market without paying top-tier resort prices.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you want a river view and a daybed balcony, choose the Deluxe Balcony River View over the garden-view standard room · book your spa time ahead in high season, since slots fill fast · and make the most of the riverside location near the Night Bazaar by walking to the night market in the evening, then returning to the calm by the river.
pros: Lanna luxury resort on the Ping River at a more reachable price than others in the area
40–60 sqm rooms, many with a daybed balcony · an in-house spa
Calm, quiet riverside atmosphere yet a walk to the Night Bazaar
Local wood and woven-textile Lanna-style décor (from the reviews)
cons: Fewer reviews than the area's bigger names
Parts of the building and décor are starting to age with use
Entry-priced standard rooms have a garden view, upgrade to River View for the water

entries.type: Luxury Riverside Resort 5★ · Mae Rim (outside the city)
entries.name: Raya Heritage
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · from real reviews · an artisanal riverside resort
entries.badge: ✨ Leading Hotels of the World · northern artisan craft
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Don Kaeo · Mae Rim · Ping riverside outside the city, ~15–20 min into town
entries.addr: 157 Moo 6, Tambon Don Kaeo, Mae Rim
entries.storyHtml: Raya Heritage is a luxury resort on the Ping River north of the city that defines itself as an artisanal resort — every woven textile, every woven basket, every ceramic piece in the room is the handwork of northern local artisans, not factory décor · designed by BOONDESIGN and opened in 2018, it was Chiang Mai's first hotel to join The Leading Hotels of the World, with 33 suites, rooms from 75 sqm, from around ฿9,800/night, scoring 9.3 · the highlights are the high level of riverside calm and the refined craft throughout, suiting people who want to step away from the city's bustle · the key honest caveat: it sits in the Don Kaeo area of Mae Rim, outside the city about a 15–20 min drive away, and you can't walk to the Night Bazaar — you rely on the hotel's car or a Grab every time you go into town, prices are high, and dining options around the resort are limited so you mostly eat in the hotel · for that reason it's placed toward the end of a list focused on walking to the night market — but if you want the calmest riverside setting and the most beautiful craft, without needing to walk to the Night Bazaar, Raya Heritage is the best in this group.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: plan before booking for the fact that the resort is in Mae Rim outside the city — it suits a getaway where you intend to stay in the resort more than head out to the night market every evening · ask about the shuttle service into town ahead of time · and allow for dinner in the hotel, since dining options around the resort are limited.
pros: Artisanal resort with local artisan craft throughout · Leading Hotels of the World
A high level of calm on the Ping River, ideal for stepping away from the city's bustle
All-suite with rooms from 75 sqm, designed by BOONDESIGN
Score 9.3, refined and personal service (from the reviews)
cons: In Mae Rim outside the city, ~15–20 min drive, you can't walk to the Night Bazaar
High prices · you rely on the hotel's car or a Grab every time you go into town
Limited dining options around the resort, you mostly eat in the hotel

entries.type: Boutique Hotel 3★ · Ping riverside · great value
entries.name: At Pingnakorn Riverside
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · from real reviews · a spacious-room riverside boutique
entries.badge: 💧 rooms from 42 sqm by the river · praised riverside breakfast
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wat Ket · quiet side of the Ping River · ~5–10 min to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 381 Charoen Rat Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: At Pingnakorn Riverside is a mid-range boutique hotel that takes the flavour of King Rama V-era architecture and blends it with applied Lanna style, set on the quiet side of the Ping River in the Wat Ket area · what many people talk about is rooms starting at 42 sqm, much bigger than hotels at the same price, and a riverside breakfast praised for its variety · it's a light-toned Colonial-style building with high roofs and wooden verandas, 62 rooms, from around ฿1,400/night, scoring 9.2 · the highlight is the value of a spacious riverside room in the low-four-figure baht range, suiting people who want a Ping riverside atmosphere without paying luxury-resort prices · the Wat Ket location is a 5–10 min walk or short drive across to the Night Bazaar side · the honest caveats from the reviews: as a three-star it doesn't have the full facilities of a five-star resort, parts of the décor and fittings are starting to age, and being on the quiet Wat Ket side you cross over to the night market · it suits people who value a spacious riverside room and good value over luxury or full facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're travelling in a group or as a family, the 78 sqm Junior Suite and 85 sqm Family Suite are excellent value for space at this price · ask for a room facing the river for the best riverside atmosphere · and allow about 5–10 min to drive or walk across to the Night Bazaar side in the evening.
pros: Rooms from 42 sqm, much bigger than hotels at the same price, on the Ping River
Riverside breakfast praised for its variety
Colonial-Lanna design, a quiet riverside setting on the Wat Ket side
Great value in the low-four-figure baht range, walk or drive to the Night Bazaar (from the reviews)
cons: A three-star, without the full facilities of a five-star resort
Parts of the décor and fittings are starting to age
On the quiet Wat Ket side, you cross over to the night market

entries.type: Boutique Resort 3★ · Ping riverside · light budget
entries.name: Lanna Dusita Riverside Boutique Resort
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.8 · from real reviews · a budget riverside resort
entries.badge: 🪵 Lanna teak house by the river · a private balcony in every room
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pa Tan · on the Ping River · near the city, a short drive to the Night Bazaar
tags: 🛏️ a private balcony in every room
entries.addr: 146 Paton Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: We close the list with the lightest-budget riverside option — Lanna Dusita Riverside Boutique Resort starts around ฿1,200/night yet gives you the full riverside-resort atmosphere · it's a teak building with a Lanna-style roof set around a green, leafy garden, with a pool in the garden, the soft sound of a fountain and the Ping River flowing past behind, in the Pa Tan area · what many people talk about is the calm riverside atmosphere that feels like a luxury resort stay in the low-four-figure baht range, and a private balcony in every room, with 30 rooms, scoring 8.8 · the highlight is the woodwork and Lanna architecture done fully throughout at a budget price, suiting people who want a calm riverside setting without focusing on luxury amenities · the honest caveats from the reviews: it's a small three-star boutique resort without the full facilities of a big resort, the wooden building and some fittings are starting to age with use, and it's in the Pa Tan area, which isn't within walking distance of the Night Bazaar — you take a car about 5–10 min · but if the brief is a stay on the Ping River in a calm Lanna atmosphere in the low-four-figure baht range, Lanna Dusita is the best-value way to close the list.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you want a river view, choose the Deluxe River View or Grand Deluxe River View, which cost little more than the standard room but give the full riverside atmosphere · it suits a quiet riverside getaway, using a Grab or red truck about 5–10 min to reach the night market · and allow time to relax by the garden pool in the evening.
pros: The lightest budget on the list, from ฿1,200/night, yet the full riverside-resort atmosphere
A Lanna teak house set around a garden, with a garden pool and the Ping River behind
A private balcony in every room, a calm and quiet atmosphere
Full woodwork and Lanna architecture throughout at a budget price (from the reviews)
cons: A small three-star boutique resort, without the full facilities of a big resort
The wooden building and some fittings are starting to age with use
In the Pa Tan area, not within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, a car about 5–10 min

advice.head: Want the calmest riverside, without needing to walk to the market
advice.bodyHtml: → Raya Heritage ฿9,800, an artisanal resort in Mae Rim outside the city, Leading Hotels of the World, northern artisan craft · or Rati Lanna Riverside Spa Resort ฿4,500, Lanna luxury by the river with a spa

noteHtml: 📌 Note: all prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season — we recommend checking real prices and comparing 3 sites before every booking · the scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms · stays on the Chang Klan/Night Bazaar side are in the middle of an area that's lively after dark, so if you're a light sleeper we suggest asking for a high floor or an inward-facing room and bringing earplugs · riverside stays on the Wat Ket and Pa Tan side are quieter, but some require a car or a walk across the bridge to the night market side, and Raya Heritage is in Mae Rim outside the city where you can't walk to the night market · during festivals (Yi Peng/Loy Krathong in Nov, Songkran 13–15 Apr, New Year) prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book 1–2 months ahead · Chiang Mai has no metro; the Chang Klan area is walkable, and a Grab or red truck is easy, with the airport about 10–15 min from the Chang Klan area · article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying in the Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area of Chiang Mai

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best stay in the Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area?
faq.a: It depends on your budget and style · if you want a location in the middle of the night market with chain standards, Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel ฿4,500, walk out of the lobby to the Night Bazaar, score 9.3 from over 1,000 reviews · if you want a luxury riverfront resort, Anantara Chiang Mai Resort ฿8,500 or Cross Chiang Mai Riverside ฿4,200 · for a special occasion, 137 Pillars House ฿18,000, score 9.5, the highest on this list · on a low-four-figure baht budget, At Pingnakorn Riverside ฿1,400 or Lanna Dusita ฿1,200

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays in the Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at around ฿1,200–18,000 per night · on the light-budget side, Lanna Dusita ฿1,200 and At Pingnakorn ฿1,400 (three-star riverside boutiques) · mid-range is The Empress Premier ฿2,400, Na Nirand ฿3,900, Cross ฿4,200, Marriott and Rati Lanna ฿4,500 · and on the top-luxury side, Anantara ฿8,500, Raya Heritage ฿9,800, 137 Pillars House ฿18,000 · all prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms, and may be higher during festivals

faq.q: ❓ Can you really walk to the Night Bazaar from stays in this area?
faq.a: Yes, for stays on the Chang Klan side · Chiang Mai Marriott and The Empress Premier walk out of the hotel to the Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market · Anantara and Rati Lanna are on the river on the Charoen Prathet/Chang Klan side, a walk to the market · stays on the Wat Ket side like 137 Pillars, Cross and At Pingnakorn take a walk across the bridge or a short drive of about 5–10 min · the exception is Raya Heritage, which is in Mae Rim outside the city, where you can't walk to the night market and need a car

faq.q: ❓ Is the Chang Klan/Night Bazaar area noisy · what kind of room should I ask for?
faq.a: The Chang Klan side by the night market is lively from evening into the night, with people and shops throughout · many stays on this list have reviews agreeing that rooms facing the street or on lower floors pick up the nightlife noise · if you're a light sleeper, we recommend asking for a high floor or an inward-facing room that doesn't face the street at the time of booking, and bringing earplugs · if you want the most quiet, try the riverside stays on the Wat Ket or Pa Tan side like 137 Pillars, Cross, At Pingnakorn or Lanna Dusita, which sit on the quieter side

faq.q: ❓ If I really want a resort on the Ping River, which should I choose?
faq.a: There are several kinds of genuine Ping riverside stays on this list · Anantara Chiang Mai Resort ฿8,500 and Cross Chiang Mai Riverside ฿4,200 are five-star riverfront resorts that still let you walk or cross the bridge to the Night Bazaar · Na Nirand ฿3,900, romantic under a rain tree by the river · Rati Lanna ฿4,500, Lanna luxury by the river with a spa · if you want the calmest riverside and don't mind not walking to the market, Raya Heritage ฿9,800 in Mae Rim is the ultimate · and on a low-four-figure baht budget, choose At Pingnakorn or Lanna Dusita

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a stay in this area?
faq.a: Several of the luxury riverside stays in this article have few rooms (Cross 29 suites, 137 Pillars 30 suites, Raya 33 rooms, Anantara 84 rooms), so they fill fast · during high season (November–February) and the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festival, book 1–2 months ahead, especially the river-view rooms everyone competes for · at other times 3–4 weeks is enough · every platform offers Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a rate that way if your plans aren't fixed, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price

quickAnswerHtml: The Night Bazaar & Ping riverside area of Chiang Mai has a huge variety of stays in one location · for a location in the middle of the night market, choose Chiang Mai Marriott (฿4,500), a walk to the Night Bazaar, score 9.3 · for a luxury riverfront resort, choose Anantara (฿8,500) or Cross Riverside (฿4,200) · for a special occasion, 137 Pillars House (฿18,000), score 9.5 · on a low-four-figure baht budget, choose At Pingnakorn (฿1,400) or Lanna Dusita (฿1,200) by the river.
